2026-11-11.title: Second Wednesday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-11.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: Blessed are those invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb
2026-11-11.verse: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.
theo: Heaven bursts into song: “Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns… the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready.” The whole history of salvation is a love story that ends in a wedding: Christ and his Church.

In Jesus' parable the invited guests make excuses, and the king fills the hall with people from the streets, “both good and bad”. But one guest has no wedding garment. The invitation is free, but it must be received: the garment is the new life of grace put on in baptism and kept clean by conversion.
outline: Ask: what excuses do we give God?
Point 1 · The wedding of the Lamb
Salvation history ends in a wedding feast.
The king goes to the streets: all are called.
Grace freely given must be put on and kept.
“Blessed are those invited to the supper of the Lamb.”
live: Come to a weekday Qurbana this week.
Make a good confession before the end of the liturgical year.
2026-11-11.prayer: Lord Jesus, Lamb and Bridegroom, you invite us all to your wedding feast. Clothe us with your grace and make us ready for the marriage supper of the Lamb. Amen.

quick: Salvation history ends in a wedding: Christ and the Church.
The wedding garment is the grace we must put on.

2026-11-11.question: What excuses do I give to God's invitation?

homily: Dear friends, heaven bursts into song: Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns; the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready (Revelation 19:6–7). The whole history of salvation is a love story that ends in a wedding: Christ and his Church.

In Jesus' parable a king prepares a wedding feast for his son. The invited guests refuse to come, so the servants gather all they find on the roads, both good and bad. But the man who came without a wedding garment is put out (Matthew 22:9–13). The invitation is for all, but those who accept must prepare their hearts.

Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9). Every Holy Qurbana is a foretaste of that feast. Our wedding garment is grace: received in Baptism and washed again in Confession. This Sunday let us come to the feast with a clean heart. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus invites us to a great wedding feast. The Holy Qurbana is a little taste of that feast. Come to church with joy!

intro: The Bible ends with a wedding; the parable warns us to accept the invitation and wear the garment of grace.

sub: The prophets describe God as a Bridegroom.
Christ loves the Church as his Bride.
q: For as a young man marries a young woman, so shall your builder marry you, and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.
Let us rejoice and exult and give him the glory, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready.
points.apply: Thank God for loving you as a Bridegroom.

sub: Isaiah sees a banquet for all nations.
The king's servants go to the streets.
q: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines.
Go therefore into the main streets, and invite everyone you find to the wedding banquet.
points.apply: Invite someone to come with you to the Qurbana.

sub: The garment is the grace of baptism.
q: And I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love and in mercy.
And the angel said to me, “Write this: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.”

concl: The feast is ready; the invitation is ours.
Let us come, clothed in grace.
2026-11-11.resolve: Attend one weekday Qurbana this week.
